violations.description: OSCEs specify clinical_images but provide NO actual radiological interpretation guidance or expected findings
violations.details: Each OSCE lists image type (ECG, CXR, CT_Brain, Ultrasound, etc.) but provides ZERO interpretation framework, ZERO expected findings, ZERO systematic approach teaching. For example: CARD-OSCE-0009 'Syncope' lists 'ECG' but doesn't specify what ECG findings to look for (bradycardia? heart block? Long QT?). GENE-OSCE-0027 'Post-operative SOB' lists 'CXR' but doesn't specify whether to identify pneumothorax, pulmonary edema, pleural effusion, or atelectasis.
violations.impact: Students cannot practice radiology interpretation from these OSCEs. No learning value for imaging stations. Fails AMC Clinical Exam preparation standard where candidates must interpret images systematically within 8 minutes.

violations.description: No radiological teaching content in any OSCE despite 52 imaging-dependent scenarios
violations.details: OSCEs missing: (1) Expected radiological findings (e.g., 'ECG shows peaked T waves in hyperkalemia'), (2) Systematic interpretation prompts (e.g., 'Use ABCDE approach for CXR'), (3) Image quality assessment (rotation, penetration, inspiration), (4) Differential diagnoses based on imaging, (5) Critical findings requiring urgent action (tension pneumothorax, STEMI, free air). References cite textbooks but don't extract specific radiological criteria.
violations.impact: OSCEs are unusable for radiology teaching. Students get no practice with systematic interpretation, Australian reporting standards (RANZCR), or image-clinical correlation.

violations.description: OSCEs don't meet AMC Clinical Examination imaging station standards
violations.details: AMC imaging stations require: (1) Systematic interpretation demonstrated (70% of marks), (2) Key findings identified within 8 minutes, (3) Clinical correlation (e.g., ECG findings + chest pain = STEMI), (4) Differential diagnoses, (5) Management implications (e.g., thrombolysis for STEMI). These OSCEs provide NONE of this structure. No marking rubric for systematic approach, no expected findings list, no time management guidance.
violations.impact: Students unprepared for AMC imaging stations. Will fail to demonstrate systematic approach (automatic fail criterion).

violations.description: Clinical image file paths referenced but not verified to exist
violations.details: All 52 OSCEs reference image files (e.g., 'data/images/endocrinology/hyperthyroidism_osce.jpg') but provide no confirmation these files exist, contain appropriate images, or are labeled with expected findings. No image metadata (dimensions, DICOM tags, anonymization status).
violations.impact: OSCEs may reference non-existent images. Students cannot practice if images missing. No quality control for image appropriateness (e.g., is 'hyperthyroidism_osce.jpg' actually a thyroid ultrasound or just a placeholder?).

suggestions.recommendation: Add 'expected_findings' field to each OSCE with clinical_images
suggestions.implementation: For EVERY OSCE with imaging: (1) List expected radiological findings using Australian terminology (e.g., CARD-OSCE-0012 Bradycardia: 'ECG shows sinus bradycardia <60 bpm, prolonged PR interval >200ms if 1st degree AV block, or Mobitz II/complete heart block with P-QRS dissociation'), (2) Specify systematic approach required (ABCDE for CXR, 7-step for ECG, ABC for CT), (3) List differential diagnoses based on imaging (e.g., CXR consolidation: pneumonia vs pulmonary edema vs hemorrhage), (4) Identify red flags requiring urgent action (e.g., tension pneumothorax = immediate needle decompression)

suggestions.recommendation: Add AMC imaging station rubric to each OSCE
suggestions.implementation: Include marking criteria: (1) Systematic approach demonstrated (30%), (2) Technical quality assessed (10%), (3) Key findings identified (40%), (4) Clinical correlation (10%), (5) Management implications (10%). Specify pass threshold: 70% + systematic approach mandatory. Add time management guidance: 2 min technical assessment, 4 min systematic review, 2 min synthesis/presentation.

suggestions.recommendation: Embed radiological interpretation guides for each image type
suggestions.implementation: For each imaging modality used across OSCEs, provide: (1) Systematic interpretation framework (e.g., CXR ABCDE with RANZCR standards), (2) Normal findings reference (e.g., CTR <50%, costophrenic angles sharp), (3) Common pathologies for that modality (e.g., ECG: STEMI criteria, heart blocks, arrhythmias), (4) Australian terminology requirements (CXR not chest film, oedema not edema, theatre not OR), (5) Critical findings checklist (e.g., CT head: midline shift >5mm, EDH biconvex, SAH in basal cisterns)

suggestions.recommendation: Verify all clinical image files exist and contain appropriate content
suggestions.implementation: (1) Check all 52 file_path references resolve to actual image files, (2) Verify images match described type (e.g., 'Thyroid_Ultrasound' file actually contains thyroid US, not generic placeholder), (3) Confirm images show expected pathology (e.g., 'hyperkalemia_osce.jpg' shows peaked T waves on ECG), (4) Add image metadata: dimensions, DICOM compliance (if applicable), anonymization status, expected findings labeled, (5) Create image generation pipeline if files missing (use medical image databases, synthetic images with pathology labels)

For each OSCE, specify how imaging findings correlate with clinical presentation: (1) Clinical scenario (e.g., 'Chest pain + ECG ST elevation II/III/aVF = inferior STEMI'), (2) Imaging confirms diagnosis (e.g., 'CXR consolidation right lower lobe + fever + productive cough = pneumonia'), (3) Imaging changes management (e.g., 'CT head shows large EDH → urgent neurosurgery, not observation'), (4) Imaging exclusions (e.g., 'CT head normal in stroke <6 hours → eligible for thrombolysis if no hemorrhage')

suggestions.recommendation: Align all imaging content with RANZCR and Imaging Pathways guidelines
suggestions.implementation: (1) Use RANZCR structured reporting format (Indication, Technique, Findings, Impression), (2) Reference Imaging Pathways for appropriateness criteria (e.g., 'CT head for trauma: NEXUS criteria, Canadian C-Spine Rule'), (3) Apply Australian terminology throughout (paracetamol, adrenaline, theatre, oedema), (4) Include MBS item numbers for imaging modalities where relevant (e.g., 'CXR single view = MBS 58500'), (5) Cite Australian guidelines (RANZCR, RCH Clinical Guidelines, ACEM imaging protocols)

agent_evaluations.review_notes: CRITICAL RADIOLOGY DEFICIENCIES: OSCEs list clinical images but provide ZERO radiological interpretation content. No expected findings, no systematic approach guidance, no AMC imaging station preparation. Students cannot learn radiology interpretation from these scenarios. MUST ADD: (1) Expected radiological findings for each image (e.g., 'ECG shows peaked T waves, wide QRS in hyperkalemia'), (2) Systematic interpretation framework (ABCDE for CXR, 7-step for ECG), (3) AMC marking rubric (70% pass + systematic approach mandatory), (4) Clinical correlation (imaging + presentation = diagnosis), (5) Image file validation (verify all 52 file_path references exist and contain appropriate pathology). Without radiological content, these OSCEs fail to meet AMC Clinical Examination imaging station standards. Manual review required to determine if this is acceptable for non-radiology teaching or if content enhancement is mandatory.
